review_basis:
A genuinely fresh real project (Missouri capital project E2508, 'Replace Steam Heating Units'), pulled from the corpus_2 GitHub Release during a low-intensity corpus-hunting pass after this same pass's own first candidate (a Maine Air National Guard boiler-replacement project) yielded a real grammar fix but no usable golden. This sheet (M103) has a real detected scale (1/8" = 1'-0", unlike the prior project's own sheets) and draws new-work gas piping in a distinct GREEN highlight color against gray existing-to-remain linework -- a real, visually unambiguous new-vs-existing convention, not an inferred one. A text-anchor scan found abundant real callouts: new-work `2 1/2" G` and `1 1/2" G` (both parse cleanly, already in `SYS_ALT`) alongside existing `1" G ETR` labels (an `ETR` -- 'existing to remain' -- suffix this grammar does NOT yet tolerate, a second real gap disclosed but not fixed this pass, scoped out since the candidate actually used doesn't need it).

`trace_run` reaches a real 76.44 LF straight vertical run cleanly, and -- unlike most of this session's own recent real finds -- the automatic size/system bind SUCCEEDS: `size:{kind:pipe,nps_in:2.5}`, `systems:["G"]`, `size-binding:beside`, matching the `2 1/2" G` label printed directly beside the traced line (confirmed via marked crop). The forward stop (`dead_end`) sits at a real 90-degree elbow where the vertical run turns to a horizontal main heading toward the building's original gas service tie-in referenced elsewhere on the same sheet ('EXISTING GAS ... SHEET M101') -- confirmed via marked crop, a real corner, not an arbitrary cut. The backward stop (`ambiguous`) sits exactly where the traced line crosses a real drawn architectural line (the building's own roofline/parapet edge, visible in the same crop) -- a genuine geometric intersection, not empty space or a narrative stop; disclosed honestly that the raw `trace_run` response's own candidate-fan array was empty for this specific stop despite the `ambiguous` classification, a detail not smoothed over, though the visual evidence for a real feature at this exact point (an actual crossing with actual drawn ink) is the same standard this corpus already applies to every accepted `ambiguous`/`dead_end` boundary. Partway along its own length, the walked run passes directly through a real tee where a `1 1/2" G` branch splits off toward a nearby rooftop unit -- consistent with this engine's own established behavior of continuing straight through a tee without registering a stop, not a hidden defect.
scope: A single real 2 1/2-inch new-work natural gas (G) pipe main (76.44 LF) on Missouri capital project E2508's own mechanical plan, sheet M103, from a real elbow (turning toward the building's original gas service on sheet M101) to a real crossing with the building's own roofline/parapet edge. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the `1 1/2" G` branch that splits off this same main partway along its length toward a nearby rooftop unit (RTU-101's own general area); the parallel `1" G ETR` existing gas line running beside this new main for its own visible length; the horizontal `2 1/2" G` run this main's own top elbow connects to; every other new and existing gas run on this same sheet (multiple further `2 1/2"`/`1 1/2"` branches feeding other rooftop equipment, not attempted this pass); sheets M101/M102/MD101/MD102 and every other sheet on this real 15-sheet plan set; the `ETR` grammar-tolerance gap named in review_basis (a real, disclosed, not-yet-fixed limitation, separate from this pass's own `EHWS`/`EHWR` fix).
